title: Video to MP3 – Extract Audio from Video, No Upload
description: Turn a video's sound into an MP3 at 128 to 320 kbps, or into M4A, WAV or OGG, and keep only the part you need. It all happens in your browser.
heading: Convert Video to MP3
subtitle: Save the sound of an MP4, MOV, WebM or MKV video as an MP3 file; the video never leaves your device.
intro: Keep the soundtrack of a talk, a song from a clip or the voice from a phone video as an audio file you can play anywhere. Choose MP3 at the quality you want, or M4A, WAV or OGG, and tick the box to keep only a part, from a start time to an end time. Your browser reads the video and writes the audio file itself, so even long or private recordings stay on your device.

features.title: Private
features.text: The video is read by your own browser and never sent to a server, so a family video or a meeting recording stays yours.

features.title: MP3 at your quality
features.text: Choose 128, 192, 256 or 320 kbps: smaller files for speech, higher quality for music.

features.title: Just the part you need
features.text: Type a start and an end to keep one song or one answer instead of the whole soundtrack.

stepsTitle: How to convert a video to MP3

steps.title: Add your video
steps.text: Choose or drop an MP4, MOV, WebM or MKV file. The player shows its length and its sound format.

steps.title: Choose the format
steps.text: Keep MP3 and pick a quality, or open Other formats for M4A, WAV or OGG. Tick the box to keep only a part.

steps.title: Save and download
steps.text: Click Save as MP3, listen to the result on the page and download it.

handles: Videos: MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV, M4V and other files your browser can play.
Audio out: MP3 (128 to 320 kbps), M4A (AAC), WAV and OGG (Opus).
Part of the sound: a start and end time, typed as minutes and seconds.
limits: A video with no sound track has nothing to save; the page tells you so before you start.
The sound is read with your browser's own decoders: a sound format your browser can't play (such as AC-3 in some browsers) can't be converted.
Very long videos take longer and use more memory, since the audio file is built in memory before it downloads.

faq.question: Is my video uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your browser reads the video and makes the audio file on your device; nothing is sent anywhere. Open your browser's network panel while it works and you will see no upload.

faq.question: Which MP3 quality should I choose?
faq.answer: 128 kbps is plenty for speech, podcasts and lectures. 192 kbps suits most music, and 256 or 320 kbps keeps music closest to the original at a larger size.

faq.question: Can I keep only part of the sound?
faq.answer: Yes. Tick Keep only part of the sound and type a start and an end, like 1:05 and 2:30. Only that part is saved.

faq.question: Why does it say the video has no sound?
faq.answer: Some videos, such as screen recordings made without a microphone or clips saved without audio, have no sound track at all. There is nothing to extract from them.

faq.question: Which browsers does it work in?
faq.answer: Recent Chrome and Edge read and make the most formats; Safari and Firefox work with most videos. If your browser can't read or make a codec, the page names it and says what to try instead.

faq.question: Should I choose MP3 or M4A?
faq.answer: MP3 plays everywhere, from old car stereos to every phone. M4A (AAC) sounds a little better at the same size and plays well on Apple devices and most modern players.
